extracted.intended_audience: covered entities and stakeholders in health programs and activities (health care providers, insurers, State and local agencies, health care facilities and clinics, hospitals, FQHCs, health-related educational and training programs), civil rights advocates, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble and regulatory text implementing section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations for health programs and activities, including standards on Notice of Availability accessibility/alternative compliance, demographic data collection considerations, and the prohibited bases and scope of discrimination protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate compliance options (§92.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The options included in §92.11(d) are options, and not requirements; they provide alternate means to satisfy §92.11 without including the full Notice of Availability with all communications listed at §92.11(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities may choose to use the opt-out provision, pursue these options only electronically, delay applicability, or not pursue them at all. §92.11(d)(1) permits asking about language needs only once if the individual exercises the opt-out option. §92.11(d)(2) allows documenting an individual's primary language and appropriate auxiliary aids and services and communicating accordingly. OCR intends to provide robust review of opt-outs and technical assistance to ensure opt-out processes are consistent with §92.11(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful access and effective communication obligations (§§92.201 and 92.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaningful access and effective communication requirements regarding the provision of language access and auxiliary aids apply to the Notice of Availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities have existing effective communication obligations (e.g., under section 504 and section 1557) which may include providing the notice in an alternate format or providing another auxiliary aid or service when necessary to ensure effective communication. If an individual needs the notice in an alternate format or through another auxiliary aid or service, that would likely already be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed notice minimum font requirement (§92.11(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Posted notices must be provided “in no smaller than 20-point sans serif font.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR amended the requirement to require print no smaller than 20-point in a sans serif font to ensure accessibility of the Notice of Availability when posted in physical locations; OCR characterizes this requirement as relatively straightforward to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested accessibility features and placement of Notice of Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended various accommodations for accessibility of the Notice of Availability, such as large sans serif print (minimum suggestions previously 18-point, finalized 20-point), notice on the first page or beginning of documents, audio or video notices for persons who are illiterate, plain language (fourth grade reading level) with visual aids, American Sign Language, screen reader accessibility, alternatives to braille (large print, qualified reader), 'Easy Read' text, and placement where frontline employees can readily see it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR appreciates these suggestions and reminds entities that effective communication requirements apply. OCR declined to require additional formats beyond existing obligations at this time but adopted the 20-point sans serif printing requirement. Commenters' other recommendations (training frontline employees, making notice available upon request, proactively asking about communication barriers, prioritizing what persons with disabilities request for auxiliary aids) are encouraged and covered by effective communication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic data collection — decision and considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR solicited comments on requiring covered entities to collect additional data on race, ethnicity, language, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, and age, but is finalizing the rule without a data collection provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR considered whether entities already collect disaggregated demographic data, which types of recipients should be covered, possible exemptions (employee number, number of beds, or other metrics), types of data and definitions, frequency of submission, costs and benefits, and how a recurring civil rights data collection could benefit enforcement. OCR retains independent authority to conduct data calls and will continue to research whether additional data collection is needed in future rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards and standards for demographic data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged OCR to adopt data collection standards and safeguards to ensure programs/grantees have appropriate training and that data cannot be used for adverse actions (immigration, law enforcement, redlining, or targeting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although OCR did not include a data collection requirement in the final rule, it recognizes the need for training, technical assistance, and safeguards to protect privacy and prevent misuse. OCR will continue working on responsible data collection practices and mitigating potential negative impacts if data collection is pursued in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on discrimination (§92.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability under any health program or activity to which section 1557 or the part applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibition applies broadly to recipients of Federal financial assistance and Department health programs and activities, including Federally-facilitated Exchanges. The enumeration of specific forms of discrimination in §92.101(b) does not limit the general application of the prohibition in §92.101(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against intersectional discrimination ('or any combination thereof')
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment to §92.101(a)(1) to include 'or any combination thereof' to explicitly account for simultaneous discrimination on multiple protected bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that an individual is protected from discrimination on more than one prohibited basis occurring at the same time (e.g., discrimination against LGBTQI+ individuals of color, with disabilities, with LEP, or who are immigrants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex discrimination scope (§92.101(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex discrimination includes discrimination on the basis of sex stereotypes; sex characteristics, including intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR interprets section 1557 and title IX protections consistently with relevant case law (including Bostock v. Clayton County). OCR provides examples in the preamble to assist covered entities and will offer technical assistance. OCR declined to define 'sex' in the rule text but included a non-exhaustive list of what constitutes sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of rare or specific diseases under disability protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination against an individual with a rare or specific disease that meets the definition of 'disability' will be addressed under section 1557's prohibition on discrimination on the basis of disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR may consider further guidance and examples; for additional information, see discussions under subpart C and OCR website resources related to disability discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccination status not a prohibited basis
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to include vaccination status as a ground of prohibited discrimination under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1557 prohibits discrimination on Congress-specified bases (race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability); vaccination status is not among these bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal entities and political-classification exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferences based on an individual's membership or eligibility in a federally recognized tribal entity are political classifications and are not race-based; such preferences (e.g., services limited to AI/AN persons) are not treated as discrimination under the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule adopts by reference 45 CFR 80.3(d). OCR will apply applicable exemptions or defenses under Federal law and intends to address restrictions on application of section 1557 to Tribal entities in the context of individual complaints or compliance reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional limits — employment and patient-to-worker conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: This regulation does not apply to employment practices and OCR does not have jurisdiction over patients as covered entities; health care workers alleging employment discrimination will be referred to appropriate agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OCR receives a complaint from a health care worker alleging discrimination in employment, OCR will determine jurisdiction and refer employment-related complaints per §§92.303(b) and 92.304(a) (incorporating 45 CFR 85.61(e)). The rule is not intended to cover patient-to-worker conduct in the regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ transplantation — prohibition and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination on the basis of disability and race in the provision of health care, including organ transplantation, is prohibited under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes documented practices that may discriminate (e.g., stereotyping about compliance or social support) and will address discrimination in organ transplantation through enforcement of section 1557 and other Federal civil rights laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of clinical judgment and medical appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 does not compel clinicians to provide a service they do not believe is medically appropriate for a patient or that they are not qualified to provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR generally defers to clinician judgment about medical appropriateness and qualifications. Nondiscrimination obligations do not override individualized clinical determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of 'sex characteristics' and intersex protections
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to remove reference to 'sex characteristics' (including intersex traits) from §92.101(a)(2); discrimination based on anatomical or physiological sex characteristics is inherently sex-based and prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR treats discrimination against intersex individuals as prohibited sex discrimination and may provide examples or guidance to aid covered entities' compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit protection for pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule explicitly includes 'pregnancy or related conditions' as protected forms of sex discrimination; discrimination may include instances occurring during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or the postpartum period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR emphasizes the importance of consistent inclusion of pregnancy or related conditions throughout the rule text and will consider additional examples or guidance as appropriate.
